Daily Brief

The transatlantic relationship faced new strain Friday as the EU 'fully rejected' US threats to ban diesel exports unless Europe releases strategic fuel reserves, a move tied to soaring energy prices from the ongoing US-Iran conflict ahead of November midterms [France 24, Globe and Mail, Financial Times]. The crisis comes as Washington deploys a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East, with up to 10,000 additional troops heading to the region [Al Jazeera]. In Europe, France closed 400 schools amid escalating student protests over education funding that have injured hundreds and led to nearly 2,000 arrests [BBC, RFI]. Russia's President Putin issued stark warnings that Moscow would use 'all weapons' to protect Kaliningrad if NATO attempted any blockade, as hybrid warfare incidents surge in the Baltics [BBC]. Meanwhile, the Flydubai pilot who thwarted an apparent mid-flight hijacking attempt spoke from his hospital bed, describing how he opened the cockpit door while being attacked, allowing passengers to subdue the assailant and prevent a catastrophe [BBC, ABC Australia, Globe and Mail].

  • Captain Smit Machchhar spoke from his Abu Dhabi hospital bed in a video call with Indian PM Modi, describing how he opened the cockpit door while still being attacked on the floor
